messages:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — Elevated 429/503 trend detected for hosted-prod (us-west-2). 429 rate 2.3% (baseline ~0.1%) sustained for 5m. Root TS: 1862345678. Dash: https://dash.redwood.ai/hosted/graphs?panel=429_trend&span=5m

alex: oncall here, i'll take first look. which routes are the top contributors?

maria: /v1/generate and /v1/stream are spiking. streaming connections from tenant t-bulk-991 jumped ~x8. see: https://dash.redwood.ai/explore?query=tenant=t-bulk-991

alex: quick mitigation plan: 1) apply cluster-level soft QPS cap to shed bursts 2) disable streaming for free/anonymous traffic 3) set short per-tenant caps for noisy tenants 4) reduce ingress retry attempts 5) monitor 429/503 trends and rollback if we cause more 503s

josh: +1. i'll take global QPS soft cap. aim to reduce overall tail without dropping Dedicated customers.

alex: command i'm about to run for a soft cap (15m trial):
```bash
redwoodctl rate-limits update --scope=global --route=/v1/generate --soft-qps=200 --duration=15m
```

maria: i'll push rule to disable streaming for unauthenticated/free-tier traffic (short window):
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/stream",
  "action": "disable",
  "filters": ["tenant.tier:free","auth:anonymous"]
}
```

priya: current telemetry: t-bulk-991 ~1.8k concurrent streams causing backend pressure. recommend per-tenant cap to 20 qps and stream max 10 while we stabilize.

josh: run per-tenant command: 
```bash
redwoodctl tenant set-quota t-bulk-991 --qps 20 --streams=10
```

katie: customer-impact snapshot: 6 mid-tier customers seeing increased 429s, 2 customers reported intermittent 503s. Not yet SLA-breaching for most; marking P2. escalate to P1 if any paid prod customer sees >2% error rate or sustained 503s.

alex: applying global soft cap and scheduling tenant cap now, will post results.

sre-bot: Action started by alex at 2026-03-15T10:45:12Z — applying global soft cap and tenant limits.

alex: global soft cap applied. initial effect: 429 fell from 2.3% -> 1.1% over 5m window. live panel: https://dash.redwood.ai/hosted/graphs?panel=429_trend&span=2m

maria: after disabling streaming for free-tier, concurrent streams from t-bulk-991 dropped ~40%. note: some clients retried aggressively causing a transient 503 bump (0.08% from 0.02%).

josh: i'll reduce ingress retry config for 30s to dampen retry storms:
```yaml
ingress:
  retry_policy:
    attempts: 1
    backoff: 50ms
```

priya: checking model runtime logs — no OOM or model-side failures. KV cache hit rates steady, points to network/ingress pressure rather than runner OOMs.

alex: next steps: keep soft cap for another 30m, tenant caps for 1h. re-enable streaming for free-tier only if 429 < 0.2% AND 503 < 0.05% for 10m.

katie: prepping customer comms. flagging affected tenants and drafting a short explanation + goodwill credit.

maria: if 429s don't improve to <0.5% we'll enable a fallback routing policy (best-effort lower-capacity model) for non-critical traffic:
```bash
redwoodctl routing set-fallback --route=/v1/generate --fallback-model=rwd-llm-small --ratio=0.3
```

alex: handing active monitoring to priya for the next rotation; next oncall at 11:00 UTC.

priya: taking over monitoring. i'll page immediately on any threshold breaches and update the incident doc.

sre-bot: Incident log entry: mitigations applied — global soft QPS 200 on /v1/generate (15m), tenant cap t-bulk-991 qps=20 streams=10 (1h), streaming disabled for free-tier (temporary). Actions recorded to incident 1862345678.

katie: updated runbook to include these fast-commands and a note to add automated detection for rapid-stream spikes (filed: ENG-1234).

josh: :thumbsup:
